Review: Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk

Andy Leung

Published: Nov 25, 2026

Hotel Review, Marriott Bonvoy

Leave a comment

Listen to audio version of this article
0:00 / 0:00 Instaread
Sponsored by

Located on the North side of the Chicago River, the Sheraton Grand Chicago Riverwalk is one of Downtown Chicago’s prominent hotels. I was attending a conference on-property, so booking this hotel was an easy choice.

Sheraton properties I’ve stayed at before haven’t been kept as well as Marriott’s own brands before the SPG acquisition, but this property seemed alright, given its continued reliance on corporate events and clientele. It was also St. Patrick’s weekend, with Chicago’s famous green-dyed rivers making the stay a little more special than the average conference.

Booking & Check-in

The on-site conference made the choice for me. Chicago was one leg of a frugal round-the-world trip after the newly converted Petaling Jaya Marriott Hotel near Kuala Lumpur and the Adahan DeCamondo Pera, Autograph Collection in Istanbul. Global conflicts ruled out Etihad via Abu Dhabi, so I flew Turkish Airlines business class (A350 and 777) for 75,000 Aeroplan points.

Only conference nights were expensed, so 4 nights became 3 bookings. The two buffer nights used points plus two Free Night Awards (Titanium status and the Marriott Bonvoy American Express card), about 50,000 points each before the 40,000 and 35,000 certificates. Paid nights averaged $357 for a 1 King.

A pressurization issue an hour out of Istanbul forced a return for a new aircraft; passengers took it calmly.

We reached Chicago about 4 hours late.

Location

The hotel sits by the William P. Fahey/North Columbus Drive Bridge. An UberX from the airport took 40 minutes (about $55 CAD) and an UberXL back to O’Hare 45 minutes ($140), both paid by the conference.

With State and Lake closed for construction, Clark/Lake is the nearest station, serving the Orange Line to Midway and Blue Line to O’Hare.

The Magnificent Mile is nearby; Navy Pier and the Bean are each a 15-minute walk.

Parking

Parking is $75 a day, with some discounted rates:

  • Special Events, $40
  • Monday to Friday Mornings (5-10 AM) to evening (leave before 7 PM): $17
  • Shula’s Diners: $18

Room – Guest Room, 1 King

Despite a sold-out weekend and a 1:00 AM check-in, I got the 34th floor, level with the lounge’s upper floor.

The curved corner room faced the NBC tower; smaller than colleagues’ rooms, it felt more open.

The small bathroom had a tub/shower.

An all-day à la carte menu is offered.

A typical standard King overall.

Restaurants & Bars

Sheraton Club Lounge – Marriott Bonvoy Platinum Elite Complimentary Breakfast

Standard breakfast runs 6:30-10:00 AM weekdays and to 11:00 AM weekends, with a greeter at the door.

Food was continental quality, with pastries, fruit and cereal but no extras.

The two-level lounge was crowded; normally open 24 hours Monday to Thursday and breakfast-only on weekends, it stayed open for St. Patrick’s Day.

Entry is from the lower level only; you can exit on 34.

Views run down the river to Michigan Avenue.

Maps and attraction discount codes were available.

Shula’s Steak House

The upscale lobby steakhouse was busy with corporate bookings.

Riverside Cafe

American fare from breakfast to lunch on the lower conference level.

Link Cafe

Grab-and-go snacks and drinks, 6:00 AM to 4:00 PM.

CHI Bar

Cocktails daily, 4 PM to midnight.

Chicago Burger (Summer Only)

A seasonal burger patio with river and Loop views.

Facilities

Fitness Center

A large gym with river views, leading to the pool.

The balcony was locked in chilly March.

Pool

The large indoor pool was always busy.

Retail Facilities

There’s a FedEx Office, shoe shine and gift shop with sundries.

Conclusion

An average but solid landmark stay north of the Loop. St. Patrick’s weekend, river dyeing included, made it a great base, with plenty to eat on site.
